Playbook.name: F5 WAF — Authentication/Authorization Attack Reaching Internet Banking - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: The WAF flagged Authentication/Authorization-class attacks (rating>=4, not blocked) against the internet-banking application - forced-browsing to authenticated resources, session/token manipulation, auth bypass attempts. Triage question: is a source trying to bypass authN/authZ on internet banking, and did any attempt succeed at reaching a protected resource?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Auth/authz bypass on internet banking risks account takeover, unauthorized transactions and access to other customers' data.

Assets.AssetType: F5 BIG-IP ASM / Advanced WAF fronting JCB internet banking and public web apps
Published banking applications and their backend servers

LogSources.LogSource: F5 ASM CEF events via syslog -> logs-cef.log-* (observer.vendor F5)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: F5 ASM logging to CEF over syslog, parsed into logs-cef.log-* (verified live).

CEF fields: deviceCustomString4=attack_type, deviceCustomNumber2=violation_rating (>=4 = real attack), deviceCustomString1=security policy, requestUrl, requestMethod, deviceCustomNumber1=HTTP response code, deviceCustomString6=source geo, cef.name=violation name, event.action=passed|alerted|blocked.

Signal.Name: Auth/authz attack on banking
Signal.Details: deviceCustomString4 = Authentication/Authorization Attacks, rating>=4, action != blocked.

Input.name: $dest_app
Input.description: Targeted policy/application (deviceCustomString1) if in the alert.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Auth/authz probing of banking is high-priority even when blocked; a passed attempt with a 2xx response is an emergency.
A single mislabeled event from a normal user session is possible - confirm the attack subtype and response.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the source is attempting authentication/authorization bypass on internet banking and whether any protected resource responded.

Step.name: Detail the auth/authz attempts and enforcement
Step.Purpose: See the specific auth attack subtypes, the URLs, and whether they were passed or only alerted.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "F5" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4 == "Authentication/Authorization Attacks" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, event.action, cef.name, cef.extensions.requestUrl, cef.extensions.requestMethod, cef.extensions.deviceCustomNumber1, cef.extensions.deviceCustomString1 | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 30
Step.AnalystNotes: cef.name gives the precise violation (e.g. 'Access from disallowed User/Session', 'Modified domain cookie'). requestUrl shows the protected resource targeted. deviceCustomNumber1 200 = the resource responded.

Step.name: Did this source also attempt logins / touch auth endpoints broadly
Step.Purpose: A source combining auth/authz attacks with a burst of requests to login/token URLs is running an account-takeover attempt.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "F5" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), attack_types = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString4), apps = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString1), passed = COUNT(CASE(event.action == "passed", 1, null)), geo = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Auth attacks alongside brute-force-shaped request volume and other injection types indicates a determined takeover attempt. External geo raises priority.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows an auth/authz attack URL with an HTTP 2xx response (protected resource returned content).
Node.Result: True Positive (Auth Bypass Reached Protected Resource - IR, force session invalidation)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows repeated auth/authz violations (passed/alerted) against banking from an external source.
Node.Result: True Positive (Auth/Authz Attack Attempt - escalate, enforce blocking)

Node.Condition: Single event that cef.name shows is a benign session-timeout/cookie quirk from a legitimate user IP.
ASM policy in transparent mode marking normal app behavior as auth violations.
Auth attack from an external source but resource-reach cannot be confirmed.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-F5AUTH-DETAIL, INV-02-F5AUTH-SCOPE to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A legitimate user's session quirk (expired cookie, re-auth) mislabeled as an auth violation.

Indicators.Item: Single/low-volume event from a normal customer IP.
cef.name is a benign session/cookie condition.
No pattern of other attack types.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the benign violation type; tune the policy if it over-flags.

TruePositive.Definition: A source attempting to bypass authentication/authorization on internet banking.

Indicators.Item: Repeated auth/authz violations from one source.
A protected resource returned 2xx to an attack request.

SOCAction.Item: Escalate to IR; invalidate affected sessions; enforce blocking on the banking policy.
Review app auth logs for the source; block the source.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A staging/transparent policy or a broken app auth flow generating auth-violation noise.

Indicators.Item: Bulk auth violations of the same benign type across many normal users.

SOCAction.Item: Engage app + WAF teams to fix the auth flow or tune the policy.
Re-assess if a real bypass is hidden in the noise.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: If a protected resource returned 2xx: invalidate sessions and engage IR now.
Confirm the banking policy is in blocking mode.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Block the source; review app auth logs; check for unauthorized access/transactions.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enforce blocking on banking policies; add rate-limits and bot defense on auth endpoints.

QualityChecks.Check: cef.name carries the precise violation - use it, not just the category.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Benign session quirk confirmed; no bypass; documented.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Sessions invalidated; no unauthorized access found; policy enforced; source blocked.
